title: Korean Firm Kia to Invest $649 Million in Mexico to Begin Electric Vehicle Production in the Country
author: Alma E. Muñoz and Néstor Jiménez
content:
_This article by Alma E. Muñoz and Néstor Jiménez originally appeared in
the[July 29, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/07/29/economia/la-firma-
coreana-kia-invertira-649-mdd-en-mexico-para-producir-por-primera-vez-en-el-
pais-un-vehiculo-electrico), Mexico's premier left wing daily newspaper._

**Mexico City.** South Korean company **Kia will invest $649 million from 2026
to 2028 to produce an electric vehicle in Mexican territory for the first
time** , as part of Plan México, reported Marcelo Ebrard, Secretary of
Economy. As of today, the investment portfolio includes a total of 1,186
projects with a value of $404 billion.

> "In an era of so much uncertainty regarding the automotive industry, the
> tariffs, the new rules, et cetera, et cetera, the fact that this decision is
> being made means that this company, which is one of the most important in
> the world, is experiencing productivity in Mexico and is seeing
> opportunities, investment in the country," which, in turn, means technology,
> jobs, and economic activity, Ebrard maintained.

President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo highlighted that **" thank you very much,
this is great news. Kia's investment shows confidence in our country and the
second thing is the boost to electromobility, which means the production of an
electric vehicle and the network of stations to be able to charge these
vehicles. So, it is very, very good news."**

Ebrard, in turn, added at the mañanera that this is** "an effort that has been
made so that more and more vehicles destined for our market and also for
export are produced in Mexico."**

On August 4, at its facilities in Pesquería, Nuevo León, the company will
start up the production line for the vehicle that is currently made in Korea.

This means, he maintained, "the creation of 500 new jobs this year and 1,500
new direct jobs between 2027, '28, '29, and '30\. It is great news because it
allows us to produce an electric vehicle in Mexico with a series of very
advanced features, very competitive, with high national content."

**He specified that the national content will be almost 27 percent "and that
is going to keep increasing. It means an expansion of the production
possibilities of the automotive industry in our country."**

He stressed that "this is a priority objective of Plan México," which is to
increase national content; "that is, what is produced in Mexico."

Andy Kim, CEO of Kia México, highlighted that the company has grown hand in
hand with the Mexican economy and reaffirmed the company's commitment to
becoming the "most strategic and reliable" partner to contribute to shared
prosperity.

The Undersecretary of Industry and Commerce of the Ministry of Economy, Ximena
Escobedo, indicated in turn that the projects in the investment portfolio are
divided into what is already underway. "That is, what is already in final
phases, in planning, and already running, which have a value of $404 billion."

In turn, she stated,** "we are also advancing and strengthening this portfolio
with the President's Investment Office and we already have 13 projects that
have immediate authorization."**

She specified that the investments are in telecommunications and the energy
sector, as far as the portfolio is concerned.
